<h2>I'd like to start off by saying, Welcome to Tech School!</h2>

This post should serve as an introduction, and link repository for the basics of developing websites with HTML.
(The CSS section should be added later on today after I get some sleep. The HTML section will also have more content added to it.)

This post will be updated over time by myself, and through the suggestions of other users.

Hyper-Text Markup Language

"HTML is a computer language devised to allow website creation. These websites can then be viewed by anyone else connected to the Internet. It is relatively easy to learn, with the basics being accessible to most people in one sitting; and quite powerful in what it allows you to create. It is constantly undergoing revision and evolution to meet the demands and requirements of the growing Internet audience under the direction of the W3C, the organisation charged with designing and maintaining the language.[1]

HTML is a system of codes that format text. <b>, <i>, and <h1> are examples of tags.
These tags format the way the text is presented to the user.

  For instance:

  • <b>This text will show up Bold</b> = <b>This text will show up Bold</b>
  • <i>This text will show up Italicized</i> = <i>This text will show up Italicized</i>
  • <s>This text will show up as a size 1 Heading<s> = This text will show up as a size 1 Heading

 

Most tags have two parts, an opening tag such as <b> and a closing tag like </b>.
HTML is formatting language, this means that any text between two tags will be modified by those tags.
In fact, you could even have a webpage without HTML; but It won't look pretty, and all the text would be uniform.

Now that you understand how tags work, lets examine the major portions of a website. This is the Basic HTML Template

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head></head>
<body>


<h1>My First Heading</h1>


<p>My first paragraph.</p>


</body>
</html>

There are Three main parts. The Head, Body, and Encapsulation tags.
* The Head Portion typically contains any external references. You'll use this more often when you become more experienced.

<head></head>

  • The Body Portion will contain all of the data you want to display on your webpage. This can be anything from pictures, to text-boxes. In the case of our example code, the Body Portion contains a level one heading and a paragraph. You can place just about anything in this portion. When doing so, make sure you type your code in below the <body> and above the </body>
<body>


<h1>My First Heading</h1>


<p>My first paragraph.</p>


</body>

  • The Encapsulation Portion simply tells the computer where the webpage begins and ends. The Encapsulation Portion is the first, second, and last line of the code shown. In order to make the website show as intended, you need to wrap all code in this fashion.
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head></head>
<body>


<h1>My First Heading</h1>


<p>My first paragraph.</p>


</body>
</html>

Once you have a good understanding of the material above, you can start to assemble your first website.
For this example, we're going to use notepad because it's a program that nearly everyone has.

Each step will be linked to an image so you can follow along with pictures if you wish. (View the full album here)
The Code above, is what your final project should look like.
 
1. Open up a blank document in Notepad.
2. Start by creating your Encapsulation Space.
3. Add your Head tags.
4. Add your Body tags.
5. Insert a Level One Heading with some text in between the two tags - Use <h1> and </h1>
6. Insert a Paragraph with some text in between the two tags - Use <p> and </p>
7. Save the document as .html
8. Double click the file to open it in your Web Browser.

 
For a more in-depth look at how HTML works, please visit W3C's Introduction to HTML

  • Microsoft Expression Web - A great free program for creating websites
